assertion.name: Malnutrition and eating disorders
assertion.description: Malnutrition, including malnutrition secondary to an eating disorder, can reduce intrahepatic glutathione available to detoxify NAPQI. Acute fasting alone is not treated as an equivalent risk factor because the focused evidence review did not associate it with increased risk through glutathione depletion.
assertion.effect: Can reduce glutathione-dependent NAPQI detoxification and increase susceptibility after acetaminophen overdose.

selected_evidence.snippet: Ageing and acute fasting are not associated with an increased risk of paracetamol-related hepatotoxicity due to reductions in glutathione concentrations.

assertion.name: Supratherapeutic acetaminophen exposure
assertion.description: Acute overdose or repeated supratherapeutic ingestion supplies the toxic substrate load. Intent may be deliberate or unintentional, and use of multiple acetaminophen-containing products can obscure cumulative exposure.
assertion.effect: Initiates dose-dependent intrinsic hepatocellular injury when detoxification capacity is exceeded.

selected_evidence.snippet: Unintentional overdoses accounted for 131 (48%) cases, intentional (suicide attempts) 122 (44%)

assertion.name: Obesity and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease
assertion.description: Retrospective hospitalized-overdose cohorts summarized in a critical review reported a four- to sevenfold higher prevalence of acute liver injury in people with pre-existing NAFLD. The association is heterogeneous: obesity and NAFLD can increase CYP2E1-dependent NAPQI formation in some metabolic contexts, while other metabolic changes can mitigate toxicity.
assertion.effect: May increase susceptibility to acute liver injury after acetaminophen overdose, depending on the balance of metabolic factors.

assertion.name: Chronic alcohol use and CYP2E1-inducing comedications
assertion.description: Chronic alcohol use can transiently increase hepatic CYP2E1 content, and selected comedications such as antituberculosis and antiepileptic drugs can also favor CYP induction. These are susceptibility contexts rather than claims that a therapeutic acetaminophen dose is invariably hepatotoxic. Simultaneous acute alcohol ingestion has different metabolic effects and is not modeled here as equivalent to chronic alcohol use.
assertion.effect: Can increase bioactivation of acetaminophen to NAPQI and thereby lower the margin between exposure and hepatotoxicity.

value.name: Twentieth-century Icelandic lifestyle change
value.description: Obligate L68Q carriers born between 1825 and 1900 experienced a fall in life span from about 65 years to the modern average of about 30, and a parent-of-origin effect emerged over the same period. Because the shift appears in several independent extended families many generations after the founding mutation, the authors infer an environmental cause tied to changes in Icelandic life-style. The specific exposure has not been identified, so no ECTO term is bound here.

assertion.description: An unidentified environmental factor associated with modern Icelandic life-style is inferred to accelerate the clinical course, but the mediating biology is unknown.

selected_evidence.snippet: As these trends can be observed in several different extended families, many generations after the mutational event, it seems likely that some environmental factor is responsible, perhaps linked to radical changes in the life-style of Icelanders during this period.
